claims.claim: AC1: Repository policy defaults are exactly Codex gpt-6-sol/medium and Antigravity gemini-3.8-flash/medium with no adapter, carrier, workflow, CLI, or test duplicate as a second operational default authority.

AC2: Local run, local continue (including delegation into PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and coding REPAIR), direct canonical REMEDIATION, and coding REPAIR accept partial or complete Human model/effort overrides for Codex and Antigravity with omitted dimensions resolved from repository policy, EXPLICIT versus REPOSITORY_DEFAULT attribution preserved, and resolved values reaching native command construction.

AC3: A new PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, or REPAIR authorization never implicitly inherits the prior RUN profile and resolves fresh repository defaults, while restart, replay, and reconciliation of the same authorization reuse its exact already-bound profile even after repository defaults change.

AC4: PRIMARY remote carrier v3 validates exactly one Human request, resolves exactly one profile from canonical policy, propagates executor, model, reasoning_effort, model_source, and effort_source through self-host delivery, and binds the resolved profile into a new profile-aware durable PRIMARY dispatch identity before RUN native execution.

AC5: REMEDIATION intent v2 and REPAIR wakeup v2 provide the same exact request-resolution, workflow propagation, durable dispatch binding, idempotent replay, and changed-profile collision rejection guarantees as PRIMARY.

AC6: New profile-aware dispatch records and the per-RUN execution-profile sidecar agree exactly on executor, model, reasoning_effort, model_source, and effort_source; any disagreement, invalid effort, malformed model, or conflicting persisted sidecar invokes zero native Executors.

AC7: Historical PRIMARY v1/v2, REMEDIATION v1, and REPAIR v1 durable journals remain readable and reconcilable under their exact historical semantics; replaying or reconciling an existing identity never resolves, attaches, compares against, or persists current repository defaults, never upgrades the journal version, and never fabricates execution-profile provenance or a new native authorization; newly submitted legacy carrier request versions fail closed.

AC8: Invalid effort, malformed model identifier, missing required Executor or profile context, and profile options supplied to MiniMax invoke zero native Executors; existing MiniMax execution without profile options remains behaviorally unchanged.

AC9: A syntactically valid explicit alternate or future provider-native model identifier can flow end-to-end through local and remote profile binding without source-code registration or a global allowlist; native provider rejection remains an ordinary no-fallback execution failure.

AC10: Remote operational receipts may retain bounded exact profile selectors needed for delivery diagnosis without becoming lifecycle truth, and existing carrier receipts still avoid asserting RUN creation, verification, review, or publication success from workflow completion alone.

AC11: Frozen TASK, RUN, RunLease, and ExecutorBoundary semantics, Dispatcher exactly-one selection, sandbox and mutation authority, Runtime verification and EVIDENCE, Reviewer verdict, Publisher authority, and no-retry and no-reroute boundaries remain unchanged.

AC12: A focused regression proves that a future compatible default change can be expressed by editing only repository profile policy plus focused validation and smoke tests, without requiring adapter, Dispatcher, Human carrier schema, durable dispatch schema, or lifecycle redesign; adapter-mechanics regressions exercise explicitly injected profiles rather than duplicating the current repository default values as a second default authority.
